For every linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every linear order $<$ on the formal commutators in the letters $\alpha$ that orders the letters as in $\alpha$ and puts formal commutators of smaller weight first (within one weight it is arbitrary), if $a$ and $b$ are formal commutators…
nodes.title: Gaglione–Spellman claim on equal commutators of basic commutators

nodes.summary: The formal commutators (bracket arrangements) in an alphabet $\alpha$ are the formal expressions generated by two rules: every letter $a \in \alpha$ is a formal commutator, and for formal commutators $u$ and $v$, the bracket $[u, v]$ is a formal commutator.
nodes.title: Formal commutators

nodes.summary: Each formal commutator in the letters $\alpha$ has a value in the free group $F(\alpha)$ on $\alpha$: a letter $a$ has the value of the generator $a$, and $[u, v]$ has the value $\bar u^{-1} \bar v^{-1} \bar u \bar v$, where $\bar u$ and $\bar v$ are the values of $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Value of a formal commutator

nodes.summary: Let $<$ be a relation on the formal commutators in the letters $\alpha$ (in applications, a linear order). Every letter is basic for $<$, and a formal commutator $[u, v]$ is basic for $<$ when $u$ and $v$ are basic for $<$, $v < u$, and, in case $u = [y, z]$ is itself a bracket, $v < z$ fails (for a linear order: $z \le v$). This is M. Hall's definition.
nodes.title: Basic commutators

nodes.summary: For elements $x$ and $y$ of a group, their commutator is $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$ (the convention of the Kourovka Notebook and of Hall).
nodes.title: Commutator, Kourovka–Hall convention

nodes.summary: The weight of a formal commutator is the number of occurrences of letters in it: a letter has weight $1$, and $[u, v]$ has weight the weight of $u$ plus the weight of $v$.
nodes.title: Weight of a formal commutator
